title: Qajar-era lease of Bandar Abbas and the Minab-Khamir coast to Muscat
summary: Under a Persian firman of 1793 (lease of 1794) the Sultan of Muscat administered Bandar Abbas, the coast from Minab to Khamir and the islands of Qeshm and Hormuz for 75 years. The arrangement was contested in 1804-10 by Mulla Hosein of Qeshm and the Qawasim and was restricted to 20 years from 1855.

title: Russian troops enter Tbilisi
summary: Russian troops entered Tbilisi following the Georgievsk protectorate (1783) and the 1795 Persian sack, ending Iranian leverage over Kartli-Kakheti ahead of formal annexation.

title: Paul I decrees annexation of Kartli-Kakheti
summary: Decree of 18 Dec 1800 OS annexing the kingdom; confirmed by Alexander I (Manifesto of 12 Sept 1801 OS = 24 Sept NS; Iranica gives 21 Sept). Tehran never recognised it; renunciation only at Gulistan.

title: Talysh khan accepts Russian protection
summary: Mir Mostafa Khan of Talysh accepted Russian protection (1802 per Wikipedia), starting a decade of contested control of the Lankaran lowland.

title: Qajars retake Mashhad from Nader Mirza Afshar
summary: After failed attempts in 1799 and 1801 and a personal campaign in 1802, Fath-Ali Shah's forces under Mohammad-Vali Mirza entered Mashhad in early 1803. Nader Mirza was taken to Tehran and executed; Khorasan came under Qajar control, though local khans kept wide autonomy.

title: Russians storm Ganja
summary: Tsitsianov stormed Ganja (3 Jan 1804 OS), killing Javad Khan; renamed Elisavetpol, the khanate abolished 1805. Opened the first Russo-Persian war.

title: Shaki, Shirvan and Shuragel accept Russian suzerainty (1805-Jan 1806)
summary: Salim Khan of Shaki and the Shuragel sultan submitted in 1805; Mostafa Khan of Shirvan formally renounced Persian vassalage on 6 Jan 1806 NS (25 Dec 1805 OS, treaty at the foot of Fit-Dagh). Shaki later abolished 1819, Shirvan 1820.

title: Treaty of Kurakchay (Karabakh)
summary: Ibrahim Khalil Khan of Karabakh accepted Russian suzerainty (14 May 1805 OS = 26 May NS); Russian garrison at Shusha. Khan killed by Russian soldiers 2 June 1806; Mehdi Qoli installed.

title: Russians occupy Quba
summary: Quba occupied by Bulgakov after Derbent and Baku (1806); Shaykh Ali Khan fled.

title: Russians take Derbent
summary: Derbent's citizens rebelled against Shaykh Ali Khan and invited General Glazenap; the naib handed over the keys on 3 July 1806 NS (21 June OS). Bulgakov then moved on Baku (taken Oct 1806) and Quba.

title: Fall of Baku (after Tsitsianov's death)
summary: Tsitsianov was shot outside Baku on 20 Feb 1806 (8 Feb OS); the Russians captured Baku in Oct 1806 (3 Oct OS = 15 Oct NS; Wikipedia says 6 Oct). Hosein Qoli Khan fled to Ardabil.

title: Persian expedition to Herat (Shahdih)
summary: Fath-Ali Shah's forces defeated Firuz al-Din Mirza (battle of Shahdih, 1807); tribute exacted and Persian suzerainty (claimed since c.1801) reasserted, repeated 1814.

title: Lankaran stormed
summary: Kotlyarevsky stormed Lankaran (1 Jan 1813 OS); Mir Mostafa Khan fled. Russia held the Lankaran lowland at the armistice.

title: Treaty of Gulistan
summary: Signed 12 Oct OS (24 Oct NS; Iranica: 29 Shawwal 1228) at Gulistan; ratified at Tbilisi Sept 1814. Persia recognised Russian sovereignty over Georgia (with Shuragel), Daghestan, Karabakh, Ganja, Shaki, Shirvan, Derbent, Quba, Baku and Talysh (frontier left to commissioners), and Russian-held lands generally. Gokcha/Sevan and Erivan stayed Persian; the vague frontier fuelled the 1826 war. Art. II line: 'Adinabazar - straight through Mugan lowland - Yeddibulag passage - up to the joint of the river Kapanak with Araz - Mehri chain - boundaries of Karabakh and Nakhchivan khanates - Alagoz - boundary of Daralayaz - Iravan/Yelizavetpol, Gazakh and Shamsaddin lands - Pambak mountains - boundary of Shuragol - Arpachay'; the Talysh frontier 'at Zinzeley and Ardabil' was left to commissioners (Ermolov's 1818 commission). Art. III: 'Karabakh khanate and Yelizavetpol province (former Ganja khanate), the khanates of Sheki, Shirvan, Derbend, Guba, Baku and Talish..., Dagestan, Georgia (together with the province of Shuragol), Imperiya, Guriya, Mingrelia and Abkhaziya'. Signed 12 Oct OS = 24 Oct NS (29 Shawwal 1228); IBS 25 gives 12 Oct 1813, ratified at Tiflis 15 Sept 1814.

title: Barakzai coup in Herat
summary: Fath Khan Barakzai deposed Firuz al-Din (April 1818); the Sadozai Mahmud and Kamran then ruled Herat independently of Tehran.

title: Ottoman-Persian war
summary: Abbas Mirza crossed at Gurbulak (16 Sept 1821), stormed Bayezid in Nov 1821 and beat the Ottomans at Toprakkale (May 1822); Mohammad Ali Mirza took Shahrizor and Sulaymaniyah and besieged Baghdad until he died of cholera on 22 Nov 1822.

title: Bruce-Farmanfarma agreement on Bahrain
summary: Resident William Bruce and Fars governor Hosein Ali Mirza Farmanfarma agreed that Bahrain was 'always subordinate to the province of Fars'; London disowned it, Tehran cited it for a century.

title: First Treaty of Erzurum
summary: Restored the status quo ante bellum (1639 Zuhab / 1746 frontier); Persia evacuated Bayezid and Shahrizor; Persian pilgrims' access guaranteed.

title: Russia occupies north shore of Lake Gokcha
summary: Yermolov seized the northern bank of Lake Gokcha (Sevan) in early 1825, claiming Gulistan allowed it; Iran protested and the occupation became the main grievance behind the 1826 war. The Russian war manifesto conceded Persia's right to the district.

title: Russo-Persian war reopens; Persian counter-offensive
summary: Abbas Mirza's army crossed the Aras in July 1826 (Russia took Bash-Aparan on 8 July; Persia took Pambak/Shuragel late July). Local uprisings in Talysh, Shirvan, Ganja and elsewhere helped Persia retake most Gulistan-ceded lands in summer 1826. Because Tehran had renounced these lands in 1813, they are mapped as 'iranian_held', not as restored claims, although the war's aim was to reverse Gulistan.

title: Mir Hasan Khan and Qajar troops retake Lankaran
summary: After six days' fighting from 25 July 1826 OS the Russian garrison abandoned Lankaran (31 July OS = 12 Aug NS); Iranian forces also took Salyan. Mir Hasan Khan then held Talysh in the shah's name until Turkmenchay (Tapper 1997); a Russian recapture of the coast later in 1826-27 is asserted in Wikipedia's 'Mir-Hasan Khan' but has no date or primary source.

title: Battle of Shamkhor; Ganja retaken
summary: Madatov routed the Persian vanguard at Shamkhor (3-4 Sept OS = 15-16 Sept NS) and re-entered Ganja about 17 Sept, ending Persian possession of Ganja. Shusha had withstood a siege begun about 6 Aug.

title: Battle of Ganja (Elisavetpol); Persians withdraw across the Aras
summary: Paskevich-era counterattack: Abbas Mirza's army was beaten at Elisavetpol on 13 Sept OS (25 Sept NS) and retreated across the Aras, abandoning Karabakh.

title: Battle of Javad; Shirvan lost again
summary: Mishchenko defeated Mostafa Khan and Persian regulars; Shirvan, which had gone over to Mostafa Khan about 4 Aug, returned to Russia.

title: Echmiadzin surrenders; blockade of Erivan
summary: Paskevich took Echmiadzin in April 1827 and invested Erivan, raising the siege in July to turn on Nakhchivan.

title: Russians occupy Nakhchivan
summary: Paskevich's detachment entered Nakhchivan without a fight in early July 1827 (some sources give 26 May); Abbas Mirza retreated. Exact day uncertain.

title: Abbasabad fortress surrenders
summary: Ehsan Khan Kangarlu opened the gates of Abbasabad (built 1810 by Abbas Mirza at Yazdabad on the northern bank of the Aras, c.6 miles SW of Nakhchivan) after the Russians failed to storm it on 14 July and began a siege (Iranica: 27 Dhu'l-Hijja 1242 = 22 July 1827; Russian-based accounts: 7 July OS = 19 July NS).

title: Russians occupy Ordubad
summary: Russian columns reached Ordubad on 1 Aug 1827 OS (13 Aug NS); the Persian governor withdrew behind the Aras.

title: Fall of Erivan
summary: After Sardarabad fell, Paskevich took the Erivan citadel on 1 Oct 1827 OS (13 Oct NS; Wikipedia's text says 14 Oct). Tabriz followed 24 Oct.

title: Russian army occupies Tabriz, Urmia and Ardabil
summary: Paskevich took Tabriz (13 Oct 1827), Urmia (28 Jan 1828) and Ardabil (8 Feb 1828). Under Turkmenchay (22 Feb 1828) Russia kept Azerbaijan as security for the 10-kurur indemnity; most of it was evacuated by about April 1828 (Kinneir, 12 Mar 1828), but Khoy was held as a deposit until about November 1828 (Kinneir, Aug and Nov 1828).

cites.note: cross-check; Tabriz 13 Oct 1827, Urmia 28 Jan 1828, Ardabil 8 Feb 1828
Paskevich leaving Tabriz, evacuation of Khoy tied to indemnity instalments

title: Treaty of Turkmenchay
summary: Signed 10 Feb 1828 OS (22 Feb NS; Persian date 5 Sha'ban 1243 = 21 Feb) by Abbas Mirza and Asef al-Dowleh. Persia ceded the Erivan and Nakhchivan khanates (Art. 3, incl. Ordubad) and the remainder of Talysh/Mughan; frontier on the Aras, a semicircular Russian bridgehead on the right bank at Abbasabad (held to 1893) and the Astara river to the Caspian (Art. 4); indemnity of 10 kurur (million tomans). Art. IV line: Ararat peak - Ashagi Garasu - Aras to the tower of Abbasgala (a circle of 1.5 versts radius on the right bank stays Russian) - Yeddibulag - Mugan lowland - Bolgarchay - Adinabazar - Cikoir highland - mountains separating Talish from Arsh - chain separating Zuvand and Arsh ('the region of Zuvand is joined to Russia') - north source of the Astara - down the Astara to the Caspian. Hijri 5 Sha'ban 1243 converts to 21 Feb 1828; the Russian Old Style date 10 Feb = 22 Feb NS is used.

title: Qajar expeditions to Sarakhs, Khwarazm and the Turkmen
summary: Abbas Mirza led an expedition to Sarakhs and Khwarazm in 1832, and Mohammad Shah another in 1837 (Iranica: Persia asserted claims to Marv, Khiva and Sarakhs). Khiva/Khwarazm was claimed rhetorically but no sustained claim or administration is documented, so it is not mapped.

title: Abbas Mirza captures Mohammad Khan Qara'i; end of the Qara'i principality
summary: Crown Prince Abbas Mirza took Mohammad Khan Qara'i of Torbat-e Heydarieh by deception in 1832; Qajar appointees governed Torbat thereafter.

title: Abbas Mirza's Herat campaign ends
summary: Abbas Mirza's army besieged Herat in 1832-33; he died Oct 1833 and his son withdrew after a late-Nov 1833 arrangement with Kamran (hostage, coin and khutba in the shah's name, tribute), per Wikipedia.

title: Ottoman governor sacks Muhammarah
summary: Ali Rida Pasha of Baghdad sacked Muhammarah (Khorramshahr) in 1837, part of the Perso-Ottoman crisis of 1837-43 that led to the Erzurum conference.

title: Treaty between Mohammad Shah and the Kandahar sardars
summary: The Kandahar sardars (Kohandil Khan) accepted Persian suzerainty during the Herat campaign; Russian diplomacy encouraged the Tehran-Kandahar-Kabul entente. Date and terms not found in detail.

title: Ottoman capture of Muhammara by Ali Rida Pasha
summary: The Ottoman governor of Baghdad invaded the Ka'b sheikhdom of Muhammara, captured and destroyed the town and received the sheikhs' homage; the town was then alternately claimed and held by Persia and the Ottomans until 1847. How long the Ottoman occupation lasted in 1837 is not established.

cites.note: cross-check; alternately claimed and occupied by Persia and Turkey until the 1847 Treaty of Erzurum

title: Siege of Herat (Mohammad Shah)
summary: Siege from 23/24 Nov 1837, lasting nearly ten months; the shah withdrew empty-handed on 9 Sept 1838 under British pressure (Kharg occupied).

title: Russia founds a naval station on Ashurada
summary: After a 1838 Persian request for help against Turkmen raiders, Russia built barracks and stationed warships on Ashurada in Gorgan Bay (Iranica 'Ashurada'; other dates: 1837, 1841). Russia recognised Persian sovereignty but refused to leave until the Persian-Soviet treaty of February 1921.

title: British occupation of Kharg Island (first)
summary: Britain occupied Kharg on 19 June 1838 as a response to Mohammad Shah's siege of Herat and moved its Residency there from Bushehr. The island was held until March 1842 because of Persian diplomatic evasions.

title: Persian siege of Herat lifted
summary: Mohammad Shah lifted the siege on 9 Sept 1838 after the British occupation of Kharg and McNeill's ultimatum.

title: British occupy Kandahar
summary: The Army of the Indus entered Kandahar (25 April 1839), ending the Barakzai principality's independence.

title: Persia relinquishes claims on Kandahar
summary: A treaty with the Kandahar chief is reported (India Office Military Report on Persia) to have ended Persian claims to Afghan territory; low confidence, no text seen.

title: Second Treaty of Erzurum
summary: Negotiated 19-31 May 1847 (British and Russian mediation). Persia renounced all claim to Sulaymaniyah and ceded the western Zohab lowlands; the Ottomans gave up the eastern mountains and Kirind valley and recognised Persian Muhammarah (Khorramshahr), Khizr (Abadan) island, the anchorage and the east bank; the Shatt al-Arab itself stayed Ottoman with Persian free navigation.

cites.note: cross-check; alternately claimed and occupied by Persia and Turkey until the 1847 Treaty of Erzurum

title: Mashhad rises for Hasan Khan Salar
summary: Mashhad's residents and ulama massacred officials and soldiers on 25 Aug 1848, just before Mohammad Shah's death, and Salar made the shrine city the centre of a revolt that had begun in northern Khorasan in 1846-47. Hamza Mirza's army withdrew and Salar dominated most of Khorasan.

cites.note: cross-check; the only source consulted giving the 1848-50 day-level chronology

title: Persian troops occupy Bampur
summary: Persian forces occupied Bampur in 1849 and garrisoned it permanently in 1850; the local rulers of Dizzak, Sarbaz, Geh and Qasr-e Qand then accepted the obligation to pay taxes to the governor, Ebrahim Khan. Before this Persian Baluchistan was "practically independent".

title: Mashhad surrenders; Hasan Khan Salar executed
summary: Sultan Morad Mirza retook Sabzevar (9 March 1849) and Neyshabur (21 March 1849) and besieged Mashhad from June 1849; the city surrendered on 13 or 23 March 1850 and Salar, his son and brother were executed on 29 April 1850.

cites.note: cross-check; the only source consulted giving the 1848-50 day-level chronology

title: Babi uprising at Zanjan
summary: Hojjat Zanjani's Babi followers held part of Zanjan against the governor and the shah's army from 13 May 1850 until a general assault about 2 Jan 1851 killed several hundred.

title: Persian army takes Herat
summary: Hesam o-Saltaneh's army, with French engineers, captured Herat (11 or 25 Oct 1856; ceremonial entry 30 Oct). Britain declared war 1 Nov 1856 and landed at Bushehr.

title: Anglo-Persian War: British take Kharg and Bushehr
summary: British naval forces occupied Kharg on 4 Dec 1856, stormed Reshire on 5 Dec and took Bushehr on 9-10 Dec 1856; Borazjan was occupied on 5 Feb 1857 and the Battle of Khushab was fought on 8 Feb.

title: Treaty of Paris (Anglo-Persian)
summary: Signed 4 March 1857 (ratified 2 May at Baghdad). Art. V: evacuate Herat within three months; Art. VI: Persia relinquishes all claims to Herat and Afghanistan and any tribute, coin or khutba, and accepts British good offices in disputes.

title: British take Mohammerah and reach Ahvaz
summary: After a naval bombardment Mohammerah fell on 26-27 March 1857 and an armed flotilla reached Ahvaz on 1 April; the Treaty of Paris (signed 4 March, ratified 2 May 1857) ended the war.

title: British evacuate Mohammerah, Bushehr and Kharg
summary: The main British force left the Gulf in mid-1857 (May-June, because of the Indian Mutiny); Bushehr was evacuated in October 1857 (Wikipedia) and Kharg held until spring 1858 (Iranica). Exact dates by place are not firmly established.

title: Persian troops leave Herat
summary: Persian garrison evacuated by about Sept 1857 after installing Sultan Ahmad Khan in April; Dost Mohammad took Herat 27 May 1863.

title: Disastrous Persian Merv expedition
summary: The 1860-61 campaign against Merv (Hesam al-Saltaneh) ended in a crushing defeat, 'the beginning of the end of Iran's claims to dominion over the Khavaran plain'.

title: Tehran claims all Makran and Baluchistan
summary: In 1281 AH (1864) Iran officially claimed all Makran and Baluchistan, grounding it in Nader Shah's 1736 conquest.

title: Persian takeover of western Sistan
summary: Persian invasion of Sistan in 1865 with a governor (Hesmat-al-Molk); Persia had been reclaiming Sistan since 1772. Western Sistan, inside modern Iran, is shown in its own region.

title: Naser al-Din Shah abolishes the Ardalan vilayet
summary: In 1284/1867-68 the shah ended Kurdistan's special status as a semi-autonomous frontier province and appointed his uncle Farhad Mirza Mo'tamed al-Dowleh governor, ending Ardalan rule.

title: Persia regains Bandar Abbas from Muscat
summary: After the expulsion of Sayyid Salim bin Thuwaini from Muscat (October 1868) the lease became void; Persia appointed Haji Ahmad, formerly Salim's minister, to govern Bandar Abbas and its dependencies.

title: Russo-Persian agreement on the Atrek
summary: Russia recognised the Atrek as the boundary (about 30 miles east of the Caspian); Persia dropped claims north of it.

title: Goldsmid's Perso-Kalat line
summary: Notes exchanged 1 and 4 Sept 1871 (Alison for Kalat; Mirza Saeed Khan) fixed the line from Kuhak to Gwatar Bay, leaving Panjgur, Kohuk, Buleda, Mand/Tump/Kech and Dasht with Kalat; Britain kept treating Gwadar as Omani.

title: Goldsmid's Sistan arbitration
summary: Award (1872) split Sistan along the Helmand, giving Persia 'Seistan proper' and Afghanistan the right bank; accepted by both governments in spring 1873. McMahon's 1903-05 award re-fixed it after the river shifted; Persia's shah protested but the award was accepted.

title: Iran reclaims Kuhak after the 1871 line
summary: The notes of 1 and 4 Sept 1871 (Alison for Kalat; Mirza Saeed Khan) placed the small district of Kohuk on the Kalat side. In 1872 a joint Anglo-Iranian commission examined the line; Iran then claimed Kuhak and the British agreed the line should lie east of it. Iran occupied Kuhak in May 1874. The exact date of the renewed claim (1872-74) is not documented.

title: Goldsmid arbitration awards west Sistan to Persia
summary: The British arbitration mission under Col. Goldsmid divided Sistan: the lands west of the Helmand were awarded to Persia and the right bank to Afghanistan. Sistanis rebelled against the Qa'en chief later that year and Persian governors followed in 1873.

title: Persian forces expel an Omani claimant from Chahbar
summary: 'Abd al-'Aziz, brother of the Sultan of Muscat, seized Chahbar in January 1872; a Persian army expelled him in March (the governor of Bampur, Sartip Ebrahim Khan, had asserted Persian ownership), ending Oman's hold.

title: Iran occupies Kuhak
summary: Iran occupied Kuhak in May 1874 after claiming it despite the 1871 line.

title: Treaty of Berlin Art. LX: Turkey to cede Kotur
summary: Art. LX obliged Turkey to cede the Kotur territory to Persia; the Sary Kamish protocol (15 July OS = 27 July NS 1880) delimited it but the Ottomans did not implement the cession for decades (Kotur remained disputed until the 1932 agreement).

title: Sheikh Ubeydullah's invasion of north-west Persia
summary: In the last months of 1880 tens of thousands of Ottoman and Iranian Kurds under Sheikh Ubeydullah of Nehri took control of Sauj Bulaq and Maragheh and ravaged villages around Urmia; Urmia held out and the host withdrew after about eight weeks.

cites.note: cross-check; ~8 weeks, Mahabad and Maragheh taken, Urmia held out

title: Akhal-Khorasan convention fixes the Russo-Persian frontier in the Turkmen steppe
summary: Following the Russian conquest of the Akhal Teke, the 1299/1881 convention effectively ended Iran's claims to Marv and the Turkmen steppe; the Yomut and Goklen within Persia thereafter dealt with a Russian-bordered Persian state. (Frontier effects are for the frontier layer.)

title: Russians storm Geok Tepe
summary: Fall of the Tekke fortress (12 Jan 1881 OS) ended Akhal independence.

title: Akhal-Khorasan Convention
summary: Convention of 9/21 Dec 1881 (Wikipedia gives 21 Sept) set the frontier east of the Caspian to Babadurmaz and ended Iran's claims beyond the Tejen (Marv, Abivard, Nesa, Meyhana); Firyuza left to Persia.

title: Russia expels Persian garrison from Old Sarakhs
summary: Komarov's Russians annexed Merv in 1884 and took Old Sarakhs on the Hari Rud in 1884-85; Persia's claim there ended with the 1893 convention.

title: Persia takes Sirri and ends the Qasimi deputy-governorship of Lengeh
summary: In Feb 1887 Persia merged the ports of Bushehr, Lengeh and Bandar Abbas with their dependent districts and islands into the 'Persian Gulf Ports' administration; in Sept 1887 it dissolved the Qasimi deputy governorship of Lengeh and four days later landed a 30-man garrison, two cannon and a flagstaff on Sirri. Britain decided in Aug 1888 tacitly to acquiesce.

title: Persia ends Qasimi rule at Bandar Lengeh
summary: In February 1887 Persia created the "Gulf Ports" governorate (Bushehr, Lengeh, Bandar Abbas); in September the Qasimi governorship of Lengeh was dissolved, Sheikh Qazib was arrested and sent to Tehran and a Persian garrison landed. A 1898-99 interlude under Sheikh Mohammad ibn Khalifa ended when Ahmad Khan Daryabeigi retook the town in March 1899.

title: First documented Persian claim to Abu Musa
summary: A report prepared by the Persian military 'for use by the prime minister' claimed Abu Musa; Britain neither countered nor objected. Copies of a British War Office map showing the islands as Persian were presented to the Shah in July 1888.

title: MacLean arbitration (Hashtadan)
summary: Hashtadan plain dispute began Mar 1885 when Persians began to cultivate it; MacLean (1888-91) fixed a compromise line from the Hari Rud south to pillar 39 (c. 34 deg 20'N, 60 deg 55'E) with a deflection round Hashtadan mound. Not mapped as a region (extent not found).

title: Convention for territorial interchange (Tehran)
summary: Signed 27 May OS (8 June NS) 1893: Persia ceded the Firyuza oasis and district; Russia gave up the Abbasabad bridgehead and the Hissar oasis near Lotfabad, and the frontier east of Babadurmaz to Afghanistan was delimited. Hissar is not mapped because its extent is uncertain.

title: Holdich line (Kuhak to Malik Siah)
summary: Agreement of 27 Dec 1895, proces-verbal of 24 March 1896 and demarcation agreement of 26 March 1896 formally included Kuhak in Iran; 11 pillars to Gorani. Boundary beyond pillar 11 left open.

title: Khaz'al becomes Sheikh of Mohammerah
summary: Khaz'al Khan succeeded his assassinated brother Mazal as sheikh of Mohammerah in June 1897 and built a semi-independent realm in Khuzestan under British protection.

title: Competing flag-raising on the Tunbs and Abu Musa
summary: July 1903: the British Resident had the shaikh of Sharjah plant his flag on Greater Tonb to pre-empt a Persian move; March 1904: a Persian customs contingent landed, removed the Sharjah flags, raised the Persian standard and posted two riflemen at each site (a Belgian customs official in Persian service is named in some accounts); 14 June 1904: Persia withdrew 'subject to the reservations' (the 'status quo agreement'); the Tunbs were then administered by Sharjah (1904-21) and Ras al-Khaimah (1921-71).

title: McMahon Sistan arbitration
summary: McMahon's award (Nov 1903) fixed the Helmand/Nad Ali line; 90 pillars placed by 15 May 1905. Accepted by Afghanistan; Mozaffar al-Din Shah protested from Europe but the line stands.

title: Ottoman encroachments on Persian border districts
summary: From about 1905 to 1912 Ottoman troops repeatedly occupied Persian frontier districts (reported at Urmia/Sauj Bulaq, Zohab/Mehran and Kotur; details are thin); the 21 Dec 1911 Tehran frontier agreement set up the commission that produced the 1913 Protocol. The occupied districts inside modern Iran are shown as their own region.

title: Anglo-Iranian agreement on Mirjaveh
summary: The UK withdrew its claim to Mirjaveh; Iran allowed the British post at Padaha to take water.

title: Ottoman troops occupy Persian frontier districts
summary: Beginning 23 May 1906 at Behik in Baradost, Ottoman troops occupied Dasht, Mergever, Sardasht and other districts from south-west of Sauj Bulaq to west of Khoy, collected taxes near Urmia and re-occupied Mergever on 3 Aug 1907. Russian and British pressure and a frontier commission pushed them back around 1911-12.

title: Tabriz resists Mohammad Ali Shah's coup
summary: Constitutionalists led by Sattar Khan and Baqer Khan held Tabriz against a royalist siege from the shah's coup (23 June 1908) until Russian troops entered on 30 April 1909.

title: Constitutionalists seize Rasht and Isfahan
summary: In January 1909 constitutionalist forces took Rasht and Bakhtiari khans took Isfahan; columns from Gilan and Isfahan then marched on Tehran. Months are approximate.

title: Sayyed Abd al-Hosayn Lari's revolt in Larestan
summary: A pro-constitution mujtahid proclaimed a revolt in 1909, issued his own stamps and, per Iranica, ruled Larestan until spring 1915, when Qavam al-Molk's force sent by the governor-general of Fars pacified it. Continuity of control between 1909 and 1915 is uncertain.

title: Russian troops occupy Tabriz (and land at Anzali)
summary: On 20 April 1909 Britain, France and Russia agreed to Russian intervention; Gen. Snarski's force occupied Tabriz on 30 April 1909 and Russian troops landed at Anzali and advanced on Qazvin. Russia kept troops in Tabriz, Gilan and Khorasan to 1918.

cites.note: cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915

title: Constitutionalist forces take Tehran
summary: Gilani and Bakhtiari columns took Tehran on 13 July 1909 and deposed Mohammad Ali Shah, ending the rebel-held phases at Rasht and Isfahan.

title: Salar al-Dowleh's revolt in the west
summary: After Mohammad Ali Shah's return attempt, his brother occupied Sanandaj by 17 July 1911 and took Kermanshah and Hamadan with tribal levies; he won near Malayer but was decisively beaten at Saveh by Amir Mofakham Bakhtiari and then held the Kermanshah-Kurdistan area until Farman Farma's 1912 expedition drove him out (he fled in July 1912 to Luristan and Kurdistan). A first revolt in 1907 was routed at Nehavand (Iranica). Mohammad Ali Shah's own July 1911 landing near Astarabad was defeated within weeks and is not mapped. Duration of control of each town is not established.

title: Constantinople Protocol
summary: Signed 4 Nov OS (17 Nov NS) 1913: detailed delimitation of the whole Turco-Persian frontier except ~40 miles at Kotur. The Shatt al-Arab remained Ottoman except Persian islands near Abadan and the Muhammarah anchorage; Persia evacuated the Zohab 'Transferred Territory'. Persia later challenged its validity.

title: Persia hands over the Zohab Transferred Territory
summary: Persian forces left the area east of the Sirwan transferred to the Ottomans under the 1913 Protocol; the commission completed demarcation by Oct 1914 except near Kotur.

title: Ottoman forces briefly take Urmia and Tabriz
summary: Ottoman volunteers took Urmia on 4 Jan 1915 and Kurdish/Ottoman troops entered Tabriz on 8 Jan after the Russian evacuation (17 Dec 1914); Russia re-entered Tabriz on 31 Jan 1915. Under a month, so no region record.

cites.note: cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915
cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations

title: British East Persia Cordon is formed
summary: In July 1915 a small force on the Baluchistan frontier became the East Persia Cordon against German infiltration toward Afghanistan; from March 1916 it was the Seistan Force (Dyer from Feb 1916), later extended to Meshed and the Transcaspian line.

cites.note: cross-check; formation July 1915, Seistan Force from March 1916, last elements out Nov 1920

title: Tangestani attack on the British Residency at Bushehr
summary: Rais Ali Delvari and the Tangestanis, encouraged by the German agent Wassmuss, attacked the Residency on 12 July 1915; the British occupied Bushehr on 8 Aug.

title: British occupation of Bushehr
summary: British troops took over Bushehr's government on 8 Aug 1915, disarming the gendarmerie; the occupation ended by agreement on 16 Oct 1915, and Persian postal authorities resumed on 18 Oct.

title: Kuchek Khan's Jangalis take to the forests of Gilan
summary: Mirza Kuchek Khan began the Jangali movement in October 1915 to free Gilan of the Russian army; it later controlled much of Gilan's administration (1917) and survived until December 1921.

title: Nationalist government at Kermanshah
summary: Nationalists who had left Tehran formed a Committee/National Government at Qom and then Kermanshah (Nezam al-Saltaneh Mafi) allied with the Central Powers; it was driven out by the Russian entry into Kermanshah on 26 Feb 1916, returned with the Ottomans in July 1916 and collapsed in March 1917.

title: Pro-German Gendarmerie seizes Shiraz
summary: On 10 Nov 1915 the Fars Gendarmerie, aided by Democrat Party radicals, seized Shiraz and arrested the British consul and colony, expelling the British-backed acting governor Qavam al-Molk; the city returned to the Qavam family and the pro-British gendarmes in April 1916 and Sykes's South Persia Rifles arrived in November 1916.

title: Baratov's Russian expedition takes Hamadan and Kermanshah
summary: The Russian Caucasian Cavalry Corps landed at Anzali (Oct 1915), took Hamadan in December 1915 (3 or 15 Dec) and entered Kermanshah on 26 Feb 1916, then Sanandaj and Bijar on 1-3 March and Qasr-e Shirin in May.

cites.note: cross-check; Russian entry to Kermanshah 26 Feb 1916
cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations

title: South Persia Rifles raised and disbanded
summary: Sir Percy Sykes landed at Bandar Abbas in March 1916 to raise a British-officered force of up to 11,000 men; brigades sat at Shiraz, Kerman and Bandar Abbas by December 1916; the force was disbanded in 1921 and some personnel entered the new Iranian army.

title: Ottoman XIII Corps retakes Kermanshah and Hamadan
summary: Ali Ihsan's XIII Corps took Kermanshah on 2 July and Hamadan on 10 Aug 1916, forcing Baratov north; the Ottomans held Kermanshah until the retreat after Baghdad's fall (March 1917).

cites.note: cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations
cross-check; Russian entry to Kermanshah 26 Feb 1916

title: Russian troops evacuate Persia
summary: After the Bolshevik revolution most Russian troops left Persia between January and March 1918; the last Russians left Tabriz on 28 Feb 1918, while a few under Baratov entered British service.

cites.note: cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915

title: Dunsterforce enters Persia
summary: Maj.-Gen. Dunsterville's advance party reached Hamadan in Feb 1918; Dunsterforce held the road from Mesopotamia to Anzali, fought at Manjil (Aug 1918), held Baku 18 Aug-14 Sept and was disbanded on 17 Sept 1918 when Norperforce took over.

title: Ottoman reoccupation of Tabriz, Salmas and Urmia
summary: Ottoman IV Corps entered Tabriz on 8 June 1918 (another date: 18 June), took Dilman (Salmas) on 18 June and Urmia on 31 July 1918; they withdrew after the Armistice of Mudros (30 Oct 1918).

cites.note: cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations
cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915

title: Norperforce formed
summary: The British North Persia Force (HQ Qazvin; main body at Manjil; a battalion at Zanjan) was formed on 16 Sept 1918 with about 6,000 men to hold the Hamadan-Qazvin-Anzali route.

title: Khiabani's rising in Tabriz
summary: Armed supporters of Sheikh Mohammad Khiabani gathered on 7 April 1920, the Swedish-officered police left and the Democrats proclaimed Azadistan; the bazaar closed in support on 9 April.

title: Soviet landing at Anzali and proclamation of the Soviet Republic of Gilan
summary: The Red Army landed at Anzali on 18 May 1920; Kuchek Khan's Jangalis welcomed it and the Soviet Republic of Gilan was proclaimed at Rasht on 4-6 June 1920 (Iranica: 5-6 June; Wikipedia: 4 June).

title: Khiabani's movement crushed
summary: Cossack forces entered Tabriz on 14 Sept 1920 and Khiabani was found and killed.

title: Last British elements leave eastern Persia
summary: The last elements of the Seistan Force/East Persia Cordon withdrew from Persia in November 1920; British troops remained at Khash in Sarhad until 1 March 1924.

cites.note: cross-check; formation July 1915, Seistan Force from March 1916, last elements out Nov 1920

title: Treaty of Friendship (Moscow)
summary: Art. III provided for return of Firyuza to Persia and Soviet recognition of Persia's islands off the Astrabad coast; Firyuza was never returned.

title: Reza Khan's Luristan campaigns
summary: The army deployed to Luristan in April 1921, took Borujerd (Oct 1923) and Khorramabad (Nov 1923), faced a revolt in May 1924, fought its last major engagement in 1926 and, per Wikipedia, had direct control by 1928; Iranica says the war lasted to 1933 although migration was banned from 1929.

title: Norperforce completely withdrawn
summary: On 21 April 1921 Norperforce was withdrawn into Mesopotamia, leaving its small arms, artillery and transport to the Persian Cossacks.

title: Red Army leaves Gilan; Reza Khan's forces take Rasht
summary: After the Persian-Soviet treaty of 26 Feb 1921 the Red Army left Gilan on 8 Sept 1921 and Reza Khan's army seized the province in October; Kuchek Khan died in December 1921.

title: Col. Pesyan killed; Khorasan returns to Tehran
summary: Pesyan died fighting Kurdish forces under Sardar Mo'azzaz Bojnurdi, acting for Qavam al-Saltaneh, near Quchan on 3 Oct 1921; the Gendarmerie regime in Khorasan collapsed.

title: Lahuti's gendarmerie revolt at Tabriz
summary: Maj. Abolqasem Lahuti, with dissident gendarmes, occupied Sufian on 30 Jan 1922, marched into Tabriz the next day and arrested the governor; the movement was crushed on about 10 Feb 1922 and he crossed the Aras to Soviet Azerbaijan. At roughly 11 days it is under the one-month threshold, so no region record is made.

title: Simko defeated and flees to Iraq
summary: Reza Khan's army (about 10,000) defeated Simko in summer 1922 and took Chehriq; Simko fled across the frontier. He returned under pardon, rebelled again in 1926 and was killed at Ushnu on 30 June 1930. Month of the 1922 defeat varies in sources.

title: Shahsevan pacified and disarmed
summary: Iranica: in winter and spring 1922-23 the Shahsevan were among the first major tribal groups pacified and disarmed by Reza Khan's army.

title: British hand Khash to Iran
summary: A ceremony on 1 March 1924 ended the British occupation of Iranian Baluchistan: Salar Amjad thanked the British and the Union Jack at Khash was replaced by the Iranian flag.

title: Reza Khan ends Sheikh Khaz'al's rule
summary: Reza Khan mobilised about 15,000 troops around Khuzestan; Khaz'al submitted at Ahvaz on 6 Dec 1924, was pardoned on 19 Dec and was seized on his yacht on 18 April 1925.

title: Army disarms the Turkmen of the Gorgan plain
summary: In 1925 army contingents were sent to establish order and disarm the Turkmen tribes, and some were forced to settle at Gonbad-e Qabus.

title: Bojnurd bombed; end of the Kurdish ilkhani system in Khorasan
summary: Reza Khan's army bombed Bojnurd on 18 May 1925, the turning point in the destruction of the Shadlu/Za'faranlu ilkhanis; forced settlement followed from 1929.

title: Ararat rebellion
summary: Kurdish revolt (1927-30) on Mount Ararat, using the Persian side; Turkish forces entered the border zone in 1930 with Persian consent. Context for the 1932 border swap.

title: Persian protest to Britain and the League over Bahrain
summary: Persian note protested the Anglo-Saudi Treaty of Jeddah (20 May 1927) and insisted Bahrain was incontestably Persian; copied to the League of Nations.

title: Jahanbani's Baluchistan campaign
summary: Gen. Amanollah Jahanbani's army defeated Dost Mohammad Khan Baluch in the winter of 1928-29; he was pardoned on condition of living in Tehran, escaped and was hanged for murder on 16 Jan 1930.

title: End of the walis of Pusht-e Kuh
summary: Iranica: the quasi-autonomous walis of Pusht-e Kuh ruled "until about 1929", after which migration of the tribes was banned.

title: Southern tribal rising of 1929
summary: From the end of April 1929 the Khamseh Baharlu (Darab, Fasa) and then the Qashqai rose; by June the rebels held the roads and most of Fars outside the cities and had Shiraz under siege; Boir Ahmad, Khamseh and Bakhtiari groups joined. The government agreed amnesty terms in July-August 1929.

title: Tang-e Tamradi: Boir Ahmad and Mamasani defeat the army
summary: In August 1930 the Boir Ahmad coalition with Mamasani chief Emamqoli Khan inflicted heavy losses (about 400 soldiers killed) on Reza Shah's advancing army at Tang-e Tamradi.

title: Boir Ahmad khans executed; military government
summary: The Boir Ahmad khans surrendered and were executed in 1932; a local military government then imposed order for about a decade.

title: Qashqai revolt of 1932 and death of Soulat al-Dowleh
summary: The Qashqai rebelled in 1932, Soulat al-Dowleh was arrested and killed in 1933, and the Shah's mechanised army cut migration routes.

title: Tehran Agreement on the Turkish-Persian frontier
summary: Pushed the line east so Turkey got complete control of Little Ararat (about 60 sq mi) and about 90 sq mi near Kotur; Iran got about 80 sq mi between Bajirga and Kuner Kota Dagh and a small strip near Lake Borolan (Iranica). IBS 28 describes the Kotur and Bajirge exchanges as in Iran's favour, which conflicts with Iranica; Iranica is followed. Rectified 26 May 1937 near Deir Marbishu (Iran's favour). The Bajirga and Borolan gains are not mapped because their location is uncertain. Sources conflict: IBS 28 and Mojtahed-Zadeh (quoted in Wikipedia 'Ararat rebellion': 'as compensation, Persia gained ninety square miles in the neighbourhood of Qotur') put Qotur in Iran's favour, whereas Iranica (Schofield) says the line was pushed east 'so as to leave Turkey an additional ninety square miles in the neighbourhood of Kotur' with Persia compensated near Lake Borolan and by ~80 sq mi between Bajirga and Kuner Kota Dagh; the Wikipedia sentence looks like a garbled reading of Iranica. Iranian-language scholarship (e.g. Jam-e Jam, 'Treaty of 1310') puts Iran's loss at ~800 km2 and denies a real exchange. This map follows Iranica; the Kotur strip is low confidence.

title: Bakhtiari khans detribalised
summary: Ilkhani and ilbegi titles were abolished in 1933, several khans were arrested and some executed in 1934 and the tribal territory was divided between Isfahan and Khuzestan in 1936.

title: Iraq complains to the League; Iran contests the 1847 and 1913 regimes
summary: Iraq's complaint before the League Council produced Iranian challenges to the validity of the Erzurum Treaty and Constantinople Protocol and led to the 1937 treaty.

title: British abandon Henjam at Reza Shah's request
summary: The British coaling station and naval base at Henjam was abandoned in 1935 at the request of Reza Shah, operations moving to Bahrain.

title: Altay award (Hashtadan plains, Musa Abad)
summary: Turkish General Fahreddin Altay delimited the 250-mile central segment (pillars 40-87, passing Musaabad, Yezdan, Kuh-i-Siah) and the Hari Rud north end. Parcels moved are not mapped (areas not found).

title: Iran-Iraq frontier treaty (Tehran)
summary: Reaffirmed the 1913 Protocol and 1914 minutes except off Abadan, where the boundary moved to the thalweg (Choteit island to Jetty No. 1).

title: Anglo-Soviet invasion and occupation of Iran
summary: British and Soviet forces invaded on 25 Aug 1941: the Soviets took Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Gorgan and Khorasan, the British Khuzestan and the road to Hamadan. Both entered Tehran on 17 Sept 1941 and withdrew to their zones by 17 Oct; Iranian administration continued. The Tripartite Treaty (29 Jan 1942) declared the troops were not an occupation and required withdrawal within six months of the war's end.

title: Reza Shah abdicates; tribes recover autonomy
summary: After the abdication on 16 Sept 1941 the Qashqai brothers returned to Fars, the Boir Ahmad tribal system "rebounded with amazing vigor" and Kurdish leaders in the Soviet zone rearmed; general accounts also have Lur and Bakhtiari nomadism returning, which is not documented in detail here.

title: Democrats seize Tabriz; Azerbaijan Autonomous Government proclaimed
summary: The Democratic Party of Azerbaijan, protected by Soviet troops that blocked the Iranian army, took power in Tabriz around 20-21 Nov 1945 and proclaimed the Autonomous Government of Azerbaijan under Ja'far Pishevari on 12 Dec 1945.

title: Qazi Muhammad inaugurates the Kurdish people's government at Mahabad
summary: Iranica ('Azarbaijan v', citing Eagleton and Roosevelt) dates Qazi Muhammad's inauguration of the Kurdish Republic at Mahabad to 15 December 1945, three days after the Azerbaijan autonomous government was proclaimed; the formal proclamation of the Republic and his presidency are usually dated 22 Jan 1946.

title: Republic of Mahabad formally proclaimed (22 Jan 1946)
summary: The Kurdistan Republic under Qazi Muhammad was proclaimed at Mahabad on 22 Jan 1946, covering Mahabad, Bukan, Naghadeh, Piranshahr and Oshnavieh.

title: British (and US) troops leave Iran
summary: British and American forces left Iran by the 2 March 1946 deadline of the Tripartite Treaty (British began withdrawing in January).

title: Soviet troops evacuate Mashhad, Shahrud and Semnan
summary: Under the Soviet communique of 25 Feb 1946, the evacuation of the Soviet garrisons of Mashhad, Shahrud and Semnan began on 2 March 1946 (the Tripartite Treaty deadline); the Soviets reported it finished by 24-25 March 1946, while troops stayed in Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran and Gorgan until May. Iranica's statement that the Soviets left Khorasan in 'the winter of 1943' is not supported by these contemporary records.

cites.note: Soviet statement that evacuation of Meshed, Shahrud and Semnan, begun 2 Mar 1946, was finished

title: Soviet troops leave northern Iran
summary: The Soviets missed the 2 March deadline; after pressure (UNSC) and the Qavam-Soviet agreement of 4 April they announced withdrawal on 24 March and were gone by about 6-9 May 1946. The garrisons of Mashhad, Shahrud and Semnan had already been evacuated between 2 and 24 March 1946.

title: Southern tribes' revolt against the Qavam government
summary: In September 1946 the Qashqai-led "National Movement of the South" rose, seizing Kazerun and Abadeh and threatening Shiraz until the Tudeh ministers were dismissed in October.

title: Iranian army enters Tabriz
summary: Iranian forces began advancing on 9 Dec 1946 and entered Tabriz on 12-13 Dec as Pishevari fled to Baku, ending the Azerbaijan People's Government.

title: Iranian army enters Mahabad
summary: Isolated after the Soviet withdrawal and the fall of Tabriz, Mahabad was entered by the Iranian army on 15-17 Dec 1946, ending the republic.

title: Qashqai Four Brothers exiled
summary: After supporting Mosaddeq the four Qashqai brothers were exiled and their property confiscated in 1954; the confederacy's autonomy ended, and in 1963 the government declared tribes non-existent.

title: Iran-USSR frontier and financial agreement
summary: Signed at Tehran (in force 20 May 1955). Changes in Iran's favour at the Moghan steppe, Dyman, Yedi Evlar island at the Astara mouth, Sarakhs (about 10 sq mi west of the Hari Rud) and a compromise Atrek delta line; Namin adjusted to Soviet gain; Soviet possession of Firyuza confirmed, ending Iran's claim. Parcels other than Firuzeh not mapped (areas small, coordinates not found). Further 1957 demarcation and 1970 Aras reservoir protocol.

title: Majlis declares Bahrain the 14th province
summary: Iran formally designated Bahrain its fourteenth province (law of 11-12 Nov 1957).

title: Iran-Pakistan boundary agreement
summary: Signed at Tehran; confirms the 1871, 1895 and 1896 lines with new sections from Gwatar Bay to Kuhak and from pillar 11 to Malik Siah; demarcated Feb-May 1958 and Oct 1958-Feb 1959; final protocol 8 Dec 1959. No territory changed hands.

title: Boir Ahmad khans' revolt against land reform
summary: In 1962-63 two Boir Ahmad khans resisted land division, ambushed a column in the Gachina/Gochestan pass and were crushed in June 1963; leaders were executed. The revolt did not hold ground for a month and is not mapped separately.

title: Iran abrogates the 1937 treaty
summary: Iran repudiated the 1937 treaty, stopped paying Iraq dues and escorted ships down the river (Joint Operation Arvand, 22-25 Apr 1969), claiming the thalweg as the frontier.

title: UN good-offices mission to Bahrain
summary: Guicciardi mission 29 March-18 April 1970; report circulated 30 April found Bahrainis virtually unanimous for full independence; Security Council Res. 278 endorsed it on 11 May.

title: Iran-USSR protocol on the Aras reservoirs
summary: Supplementary protocol of 7 May 1970 to the 1954 agreement redelimited the boundary in the Aras along the Araks hydro-electric dam reservoir near Nakhchivan (41 miles, 14 turning points) and the Mil-Mugan water-intake reservoir (1.95 miles, four turning points). Land-area effect not stated; not mapped. The 1957 demarcation (3 m no-man's land on each side) had already shifted the Moghan line north-eastward at Soviet expense.

title: Iran renounces its claim to Bahrain
summary: The Majlis approved the UN report 184-4 on 14 May 1970, the Senate unanimously on 18 May; Bahrain became independent 15 Aug 1971. Tehran date chosen: Majlis vote.

title: Iran-Sharjah memorandum on Abu Musa
summary: MoU on shared administration of Abu Musa (signed 29 Nov or 30 Nov 1971 depending on source; Iranian troops in the northern sector, Sharjah police elsewhere); Iranian forces landed on 30 Nov.

title: Iran seizes the Tunbs
summary: After the British withdrawal Iranian forces landed on Greater and Lesser Tunb (30 Nov 1971; some sources say the evening of 29 Nov). There was an armed clash on Greater Tunb (Wikipedia: four Ras al-Khaimah policemen and three Iranian soldiers killed) and the inhabitants were deported to Ras al-Khaimah.

title: Algiers Accord (joint communique)
summary: Shah and Saddam Hussein agreed to demarcate the land border on the 1913 Protocol and 1914 minutes and the river border on the thalweg; Iran ended support for Iraqi Kurds. Tehran protocol 15-17 March 1975.

title: Baghdad treaty on the State Boundary
summary: Treaty plus three protocols: land boundary redemarcation, river boundary on the thalweg (105 km), border security. Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad were to pass to Iraq but were never handed over; their exact location is uncertain, so they are not mapped.

title: Islamic Revolution
summary: The fall of the monarchy on 11 Feb 1979 collapsed state authority in several peripheral regions for weeks to months.

title: Kurdish groups seize garrisons in Sanandaj, Paveh, Saqqez, Marivan and Mahabad
summary: In mid-March 1979 Kurdish factions took the police headquarters and army bases in Sanandaj (17-19 March), Paveh, Saqqez and Marivan; Mahabad was in Kurdish hands from early March.

title: Khomeini's jihad: Iranian offensive retakes Kurdish towns
summary: After Khomeini's jihad declaration on 17 Aug 1979 the army took Sanandaj and Saqqez (by 1 Sept), Mahabad (3 Sept) and Sardasht, Bukan and Piranshahr (4-6 Sept). The KDPI retook Mahabad on 20 Oct 1979.

title: Qashqai insurgency of Khosrow Khan
summary: After an attempt to arrest Khosrow Khan in June 1980 the Qashqai insurgents defied the government for two years until a Revolutionary Guards night attack in April 1982; Khosrow Khan was hanged on 8 Oct 1982 and Nasser Khan died in 1984.

title: Iraq abrogates the Algiers Accord
summary: Iraq retook Zain al-Qaws and Saif Saad on 10 Sept 1980, Iran declared the accord void 14 Sept and Saddam abrogated it on 17 Sept, five days before the invasion. Tehran maintains the thalweg claim.

title: Iraq invades Iran
summary: Iraq attacked on 22 Sept 1980 across a 400-mile front, taking Qasr-e Shirin, Mehran and a salient in Khuzestan; by December 1980 only parts of Khuzestan were occupied.

title: Siege of Abadan lifted
summary: Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh broke the siege of Abadan that had begun in late 1980.

title: Khorramshahr liberated
summary: Iranian forces retook Khorramshahr on 24 May 1982 (Operation Beit ol-Moqaddas, 24 April-24 May), after the city had fallen to Iraq on 24 Oct-10 Nov 1980.

title: Iraq announces withdrawal from Iranian territory
summary: Iraq announced on 20 June 1982 that it would withdraw to the international border; Iran then carried the war into Iraq.

title: Iranian gains inside Iraq retained after the 1982 offensives (not mapped)
summary: Operation Ramadan (from 13 July 1982) took ~50 km2 of Iraqi land near Basra and, after Muslim ibn Aqil and Muharram (Jul-Nov 1982), Iran kept some 210 km2 of Iraqi territory; the Zubaidat oil-field border area east of Amara 'had been held by Iran since mid-1982' until Iraqi Presidential Guards retook it on 12 July 1988. None of these parcels has a sourced extent or coordinates, so they are not mapped as regions.

title: Operation Dawn 2: Iran seizes Haj Omran
summary: Iranian forces advanced from Piranshahr and took the Haj Omran highlands (~390 km2) in Iraqi Kurdistan.

title: Operation Dawn 4: Penjwin valley
summary: Iran and PUK peshmerga took the Penjwin valley (466 km2); operation ended around 21 Nov 1983.

title: KDPI withdraws to Iraq
summary: After the Iranian counter-offensives of 1982-83 the KDPI withdrew into Iraqi territory by early 1984; sporadic Komala activity continued but no territory was held.

title: Post-1983: no area outside central control lasting a month (research note)
summary: After the KDPI left for Iraq (early 1984) and the Iran-Iraq war ended (1988/1990), I found no area of Iran outside the central government's control for as long as a month. Insurgencies (PJAK, Jundallah/Jaish al-Adl, People's Fighters Front) and the unrest of 2009, 2019 and 2022 did not hold territory. Exceptions flagged in the 2026 events: a few days in January 2026 (Abdanan, Malekshahi) and ongoing 2026 Kurdish-IRGC fighting where no confirmed territorial holding was reported. No region record is made for 1984-2026.

cites.note: cross-check, Sept 2026: clashes in the Sardasht-Baneh-Saqqez triangle but no held territory

title: Operation Kheibar: Majnoon Islands
summary: Iranian assault through the Hawizeh marsh took the Majnoon Islands (~160 km2, ~50 oil wells), held until 1988.

title: Operation Dawn 8: Iran takes Al-Faw
summary: Surprise crossing of the Shatt al-Arab (night of 9-10 Feb) captured the Faw peninsula; first major Iranian occupation of Iraqi land.

title: Iraq retakes Mehran; Iran regains it (Karbala-1)
summary: Iraq's II Corps captured Mehran on 15-19 May 1986 and Iran recaptured the area in Operation Karbala-1 (30 June-3 July), defeating a Republican Guard counter-attack on 4 July.

title: Operation Karbala-5 (Basra front)
summary: Iran seized a sliver of Basra governorate near Duaiji/Fish Lake and held positions around Shalamcheh until Iraq's May 1988 counterattack. Too small to map reliably.

title: Operation Dawn 10: Halabja captured
summary: Iranian forces and peshmerga captured Halabja, Dojileh and Khurmal (14-19 March); Iraqi chemical attack 16-17 March.

title: Iraq retakes Al-Faw
summary: Operation Ramadan Mubarak (17-18 April 1988) expelled Iranian forces from the peninsula within 35 hours.

title: Battle of Fish Lake / Shalamcheh
summary: Tawakalna 1 pushed Iranian forces out of positions held in Basra governorate since Jan 1987.

title: Operation Forty Stars and the MEK's Eternal Light
summary: On 18 June 1988 Iraqi forces and the MEK captured Mehran; on 12 July Iraq entered Dehloran, Qasr-e Shirin, Sumar, Naft Shahr and Sar-e Pol-e Zahab and withdrew from the towns after Iran accepted the ceasefire. On 26 July the MEK's Eternal Light (Forough-e Javidan) reached Eslamabad-e Gharb and was defeated in Operation Mersad within days; none of these gains lasted a month except possibly Mehran (low confidence).

cites.note: cross-check; Iraqi entry to Dehloran/Qasr-e Shirin 12 July 1988

title: Iraq retakes Majnoon
summary: Iraqi forces recovered the Majnoon oilfield, 4.5 years after Iran took it.

title: Iran abandons Halabja
summary: Iranian forces left Halabja without a fight, the last major foothold in Iraq.

title: Iran announces withdrawal from Haj Omran
summary: After Iraq's ultimatum of 13 July 1988, Rafsanjani announced on 14 July that all Iranian forces would pull back from the occupied Iraqi territory north of Haj Omran, 'the last major piece of territory Iran held on Iraqi soil' (Cordesman). The Iranian news agency called it taking up new positions.

title: UN-supervised ceasefire
summary: Khomeini accepted UNSC Res. 598 in mid-July 1988 (18-20 July); the ceasefire took effect 20 Aug 1988. Iraq's counter-invasion of Iran (about 9,600 km2) ended soon after; no Iraqi territory remained mapped as Iranian-held.

title: Saddam Hussein accepts the 1975 accord
summary: Mid-Aug 1990 Iraq restored the 1975 border and thalweg and promised to leave occupied Iranian land (about 2,600 sq km, inside modern Iran).

title: Iraq withdraws from the last occupied Iranian territory
summary: On 15-16 Aug 1990 Saddam Hussein accepted the 1975 Algiers border and offered to withdraw from about 2,600 km2 of Iranian territory; almost all forces were back across the border within about five days and the UN reported the withdrawal almost complete on 24 Sept 1990.

title: Iran asserts full control of Abu Musa
summary: After expelling foreign workers in April 1992 Iran barred Sharjah's teachers on 24 Aug 1992; the UAE says this breaches the 1971 MoU.

title: Caspian sector (note only)
summary: Tehran's long-held position was equal division of the Caspian (20 per cent each) while Soviet-Iranian treaties (1921, 1940) left no sectoral line; the 2018 Aktau Convention did not fix sectors. Not mapped.

title: Abdanan and Malekshahi briefly outside government control
summary: During the Dec 2025-Jan 2026 protests security forces withdrew from Abdanan and Malekshahi (Ilam) for a few days around 6-8 January 2026 and protesters took the towns; the sources found do not give the date of restored control. Under the one-month threshold, so no region record.

title: 2026 Iran war (US-Israeli strikes): no Iranian territory seized
summary: The war that began on 28 Feb 2026 saw strikes on Kharg, Qeshm, Larak, Kish and Abu Musa and an Israeli special-forces ground raid on 2 March, but Britannica reports that no Iranian territory was seized as of 1 Oct 2026; a ceasefire in April and an MOU on 17 June 2026 collapsed on 6-7 July.

title: PJAK/KDPI-IRGC fighting in Iranian Kurdistan (ongoing)
summary: Armed clashes since 7 June 2026 around Marivan, Mahabad, Piranshahr, Baneh and Saqqez involve mobile operations rather than held territory according to the sources found; flagged for review if later reporting shows held areas.
